examples.solution_text:
The triangle shares the rectangle's $9\text{ m}$ side.
$\begin{align*}A_1&=9\times4\\&=36\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}A_2&=\frac12\times9\times2\\&=9\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}A&=A_1+A_2\\&=36+9\\&=45\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$

The semicircle has diameter $4\text{ m}$, so its radius is $2\text{ m}$.
$\begin{align*}A_1&=4\times3\\&=12\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$
$A_2=\frac12\pi(2)^2=2\pi\text{ m}^2$
$\begin{align*}A&=A_1+A_2\\&=12+2\pi\\&\approx18.28\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A rectangular yard is $15\text{ m}$ by $10\text{ m}$. A rectangular patio is $4\text{ m}$ by $3\text{ m}$, and a separate triangular flower bed has base $6\text{ m}$ and perpendicular height $3\text{ m}$. Calculate the remaining area of the yard.
examples.solution_text:
Subtract both areas from the whole yard.
$A_1=15\times10=150\text{ m}^2$
$A_2=4\times3=12\text{ m}^2$
$A_3=\frac12\times6\times3=9\text{ m}^2$
$\begin{align*}A&=A_1-A_2-A_3\\&=150-12-9\\&=129\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A path of constant width $1\text{ m}$ surrounds a rectangular garden $7\text{ m}$ long and $4\text{ m}$ wide. Calculate the area of the path.
examples.solution_text:
Add the path width at both ends of each garden dimension.
$L=7+2(1)=9\text{ m}$
$W=4+2(1)=6\text{ m}$
$\begin{align*}A&=A_{\text{outer}}-A_{\text{garden}}\\&=9\times6-7\times4\\&=54-28\\&=26\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A semicircle of diameter $4\text{ m}$ is cut from one side of a rectangular sheet $9\text{ m}$ by $5\text{ m}$. Calculate the remaining area to $2$ decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
The semicircle has radius $4\div2=2\text{ m}$.
$A_1=9\times5=45\text{ m}^2$
$A_2=\frac12\pi(2)^2=2\pi\text{ m}^2$
$\begin{align*}A&=A_1-A_2\\&=45-2\pi\\&\approx38.72\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$

The semicircle has radius $3\div2=1.5\text{ m}$.
$A_1=7\times4=28\text{ m}^2$
$A_2=3\times2=6\text{ m}^2$
$A_3=\frac12\pi(1.5)^2=1.125\pi\text{ m}^2$
$\begin{align*}A&=A_1-A_2-A_3\\&=28-6-1.125\pi\\&\approx18.47\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A racetrack lies between two ovals. Each oval consists of a rectangle with a semicircle on each short side. Both rectangles are $24\text{ m}$ long. Their widths are $16\text{ m}$ and $10\text{ m}$, and each semicircle's diameter equals its rectangle's width. Calculate the track area to $2$ decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
Each pair of semicircles forms one circle. The outer radius is $8\text{ m}$ and the inner radius is $5\text{ m}$.
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{outer}}&=24\times16+\pi(8)^2\\&=384+64\pi\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{inner}}&=24\times10+\pi(5)^2\\&=240+25\pi\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}A&=A_{\text{outer}}-A_{\text{inner}}\\&=(384+64\pi)-(240+25\pi)\\&=144+39\pi\\&\approx266.52\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A garden consists of a rectangle $11\text{ m}$ by $5\text{ m}$ with a triangle of perpendicular height $3\text{ m}$ joined along its $11\text{ m}$ side. Each bag of mulch covers $6\text{ m}^2$. Only whole bags can be bought. How many bags are needed?
examples.solution_text:
$A_1=11\times5=55\text{ m}^2$
$A_2=\frac12\times11\times3=16.5\text{ m}^2$
$\begin{align*}A&=A_1+A_2\\&=55+16.5\\&=71.5\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$
$71.5\div6=11.9166\ldots$
Round up to cover the whole garden: $12$ bags.

examples.derivation: Right rectangle width: 8−3=5 m. Non-overlapping areas: 3×5=15 m² and 5×2=10 m². Total: 25 m².
Upper arm height: 7−2=5 m. Bottom area: 12×2=24 m². Each upper arm: 3×5=15 m². Total: 24+2×15=54 m².
Rectangle: 9×4=36 m². Roof triangle: ½×9×2=9 m². Total: 45 m². Diagram marks the perpendicular roof height correctly.
Semicircle radius: 4÷2=2 m. Rectangle: 12 m². Semicircle: 2π m². Total: 12+2π=18.283185… m², rounding to 18.28 m².
Yard: 15×10=150 m². Patio: 4×3=12 m². Separate flower bed: ½×6×3=9 m². Remaining area: 150−12−9=129 m².
Outer dimensions: 7+2×1=9 m and 4+2×1=6 m. Path area: 9×6−7×4=54−28=26 m².
Triangle base: 12−7=5 m. Rectangle: 7×6=42 m². Triangle: ½×5×6=15 m². Total: 57 m². Formula check: ½×(12+7)×6=57 m².
Cut-out radius: 2 m. Rectangle: 45 m². Semicircle: 2π m². Remaining area: 45−2π=38.716814… m², rounding to 38.72 m².
Wall: 28 m². Rectangular opening: 6 m². Semicircular opening: ½π×1.5²=1.125π m². Remaining area: 22−1.125π=18.465708… m², rounding to 18.47 m². Diagram opening reaches 3.5 m within the 4 m wall.
Outer oval: 24×16+π×8²=384+64π m². Inner oval: 24×10+π×5²=240+25π m². Difference: 144+39π=266.522113… m², rounding to 266.52 m².
Rectangle: 55 m². Triangle: ½×11×3=16.5 m². Total: 71.5 m². Coverage requires 71.5÷6=11.916666… bags; rounding up gives 12 bags.
